title: Developing with 4D Server Part 3: Naming Conventions for Multi-Developer 4D Projects
author: ACI US Technical Support
featured_technology: Path to name / Path only path global functions
Cross-platform (Mac/Windows) document naming and pathname conventions

historical_commentary.text: Despite its title referencing multi-developer naming conventions, this note's actual content (TN 96-41, 'File Names and Pathnames') is a cross-platform technical guide to programmatically extracting file names from full pathnames on Mac vs. Windows, covering platform-specific path separators, filename length limits, and the MAP FILE TYPES command for associating document types across platforms. The specific pathname-parsing routines and legacy filename length restrictions (e.g., DOS 8.3 names) it documents are obsolete on modern operating systems, which support long file names and largely unified path-handling conventions, and modern 4D provides built-in, higher-level file/folder management commands (and cross-platform File and Folder objects) that make manual pathname string-parsing routines like these unnecessary.
related_updates: Modern operating systems (macOS, current Windows) support long file names, eliminating the DOS 8.3 filename length restrictions discussed as a cross-platform compatibility concern in this note
Modern 4D provides built-in File and Folder objects with higher-level path manipulation methods, removing the need for manual custom pathname-parsing routines like the ones presented here
The MAP FILE TYPES command's Mac-vs-Windows document type mapping concern is much less prominent today given modern OS/file-manager improvements in cross-platform file type recognition
